passage: I'm Tushar, and I first really noticed my mother, Ganga, when I was fifteen and found her at midnight hemming other people's blouses again. She'd done it for years so I could stay in school, and I'd never once asked how her shoulders felt. That night I said thank you, badly, and she waved it away. I felt warm and heavy at once. I told myself I would become an engineer, earn a lot, and pay it all back. Then one evening, sketching buildings in my notebook, I realised I didn't want to be an engineer; I wanted to be an architect. When I said so, she stopped sewing. "I didn't work for your life to belong to me," she said. Now I cook dinner twice a week and keep drawing.

qa.q: What was Ganga doing at midnight when Tushar noticed her?
What two feelings did Tushar have after thanking Ganga?
qa.a: Warmth and heaviness, meaning gratitude together with the pressure to succeed and repay her.

qa.q: What did Tushar do that was fair to Ganga and to Tushar too?
qa.a: Tushar said thanks and took on a real responsibility by cooking dinner twice a week, but kept drawing instead of giving up the architect dream to repay her.

qa.q: How does Ganga see what she has done for Tushar?
qa.a: As a gift, not a debt. She stopped sewing and said she didn't work for Tushar's life to belong to her.

grounding: Tushar sees a parent's sacrifices with gratitude and pressure, thanks her, shares responsibility and keeps a personal dream.

passage:
Class teacher's note, Class 12A, Monday
Harish stayed back to ask about the engineering entrance forms. He seemed tense. When I asked what he really wanted to study, he said quietly, "Music. But I can't."
He explained that his father, Samir, drives an auto-rickshaw twelve hours a day and has saved for years for Harish's coaching. "He skipped his own medicines once to pay my fees," Harish said. "I have to become an engineer. I owe him."
I told him his gratitude was real and good, and that thanking his father and helping at home were fair ways to show it. But I said repaying love doesn't have to mean giving up his own dream.
He agreed to talk to his father openly about music this week. I have offered to meet them both, and I'll share information on music college scholarships with Harish tomorrow.

qa.q: How many hours a day does Harish's father drive the auto-rickshaw?
How does Harish feel about his father's sacrifices?
qa.a: He feels deep gratitude but also heavy pressure, believing he owes it to his father to give up music for engineering.

qa.q: How did the note-writer help Harish think more clearly?
qa.a: By affirming his gratitude, suggesting fair ways to show it, and reminding him that repaying love doesn't mean giving up his dream.

qa.q: How might Samir feel if Harish talks to him openly about music?
qa.a: Samir may be surprised, but he might also want his son to be happy rather than to feel trapped by debt.

grounding: A teen grateful for his father's sacrifices feels pressure to succeed, and a teacher helps him see he need not give up his own dream.

passage:
Thursday
Amma came home at eleven again. She works at the hospital canteen in the day and stitches blouses at night. Her fingers are rough now. She still asked about my art project first thing.
I made her tea and pressed her feet like she used to do for Ajji. I said, "Thank you, Amma. For everything." She laughed and said, "Don't get emotional, Avni."
But I am emotional. Some nights I think I should stop art and do commerce so I can get a job faster. Pay her back.
Today my art teacher, Shalini ma'am, said my portfolio could get a scholarship to the design college. When I told Amma, her eyes filled up. She said, "I didn't work this hard so you would give up what you love."
So here's my plan. I'll take over cooking on weekdays and help with the stitching on Sundays. And I'll apply for that scholarship. Both.

qa.q: What does Amma do at night?
How does Avni feel about Amma's hard work?
qa.a: Avni feels grateful and emotional, but also pressured to give up art to repay Amma quickly.

qa.q: What is Avni planning, and why is it a fair balance?
qa.a: To take on cooking and help with stitching while still applying for the design scholarship, so Avni shares responsibility without giving up the dream.

qa.q: How does Amma feel when she hears about the scholarship?
qa.a: Amma is moved to tears and proud, wanting Avni to keep doing what Avni loves.

grounding: A teen grateful for a mother's sacrifices takes on fair responsibility at home without giving up the dream of design college.
